detailed_findings.finding: The nonvanishing step uses only the oddness of n; the separately proved gcd(n,2d)=1 is not needed later, but this does not create a gap.

reason: The proof correctly establishes that n is odd and gcd(n,2d)=1 from n ≡ 1 mod 2d, then shows U_{d,n}(ζ) ≠ 0 for every nontrivial nth root of unity ζ by contradiction from ζ^{dj} = -1 and oddness of n. The coprimality argument with M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 is complete: any nonconstant common divisor would yield a complex root α that is either a nontrivial nth root coming from [n]_q(α)=0 or a primitive nth root coming from Φ_n(α)=0, contradicting the established nonvanishing of U_{d,n} at all such α. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
